input.summary: The packet contains no prior protocol, and the owner message raises an unresolved unit ambiguity (seconds vs. milliseconds) for a reported flow-completion-time value. This draft cannot be completed until the owner clarifies the intended unit and value, so protocol=null is returned with a targeted clarifying question. Two additional questions address missing inputs and resource bounds needed before a full pilot can be specified.
clarification_questions: The owner message notes a conflict between 0.2 seconds and 0.2 milliseconds for the reported flow completion time change — which value and unit should be recorded as the paper's stated result, and where in the source does that figure appear?
What traffic inputs (e.g., file sizes, number of flows, TCP variant) and emulated bottleneck parameters (bandwidth, queue size) should be used so the pilot conditions match the paper's setup?

proposal.problem: The paper claim states that adding 20 ms of emulated delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed bottleneck conditions, but the exact reported magnitude is ambiguous: the owner notes a conflict between 0.2 s and 0.2 ms.
proposal.question: Under the emulated bottleneck conditions described in the paper, what is the observed difference in TCP flow completion time between a baseline (no added delay) and a 20 ms added-delay condition, and in which unit (seconds or milliseconds) is that difference expressed?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions are compared: (1) baseline — emulated bottleneck with no added one-way delay; (2) treatment — same bottleneck with 20 ms of added one-way delay. All other emulation parameters are held fixed.
proposal.related_work: The source is cited as a synthetic networking paper claim for development evaluation (SHA-256: aaaa…aaaa); no full text or prior measurements are available for comparison.
proposal.alternatives: The observed difference in flow completion time could reflect queue-induced delay rather than propagation delay alone; directionality (one-way vs. round-trip placement) of the 20 ms delay is unresolved and may affect the magnitude.
proposal.design: A descriptive pilot measuring TCP flow completion time under two emulated-delay conditions using the emulated-netem-v1 runner; conditions, inputs, and resource limits remain unspecified pending owner clarification.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: TCP flow completion time, unit unresolved (seconds or milliseconds pending owner clarification). Secondary: per-flow throughput if available.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck bandwidth, queue discipline, queue size, TCP variant, flow size, and number of concurrent flows are held constant across conditions; only the added delay parameter varies.
proposal.inputs: Traffic inputs (flow sizes, TCP variant) and bottleneck parameters (bandwidth, queue size) are not yet specified; source identity hashes for any input files are unknown pending owner provision.
proposal.limitations: The unit ambiguity (0.2 s vs. 0.2 ms) cannot be resolved from metadata alone; no full paper text is available. Simulation results cannot establish real-world performance or causality. Separate invocations do not establish independence.
